t: You're looking at an equestrian statue of Ferdinand Foch, in Lower Grosvenor Gardens. Foch was Supreme Commander of the Allied Forces on the Western Front from the spring of 1918, and he's widely seen as the architect of Germany's defeat that November. The British made him an honorary Field Marshal, an honour no other French commander received. After his death in 1929, a campaign was launched for a London memorial. The sculptor, Georges Malissard, made this replica of his statue at Cassel in France. The Prince of Wales unveiled it on the fifth of June, 1930.
